newsitem.title: IRAN: Khatami sworn in as Iran's new president.
newsitem.headline: Khatami sworn in as Iran's new president.

text.p: Iran's President Mohammad Khatami, a clergyman known for his moderate views, took the oath of office on Monday saying his government would seek dialogue with all nations that respected the Islamic republic.

"I as the president of the Islamic Republic of Iran swear before the holy Koran and the Iranian nation and God to be the guardian of the official religion, the Islamic republic and the constitution," Khatami said at a ceremony in parliament.

It was attended by parliament speaker Ali Akbar Nateq-Nouri, whom Khatami defeated in the May elections, the head of judiciary Mohammad Yazdi, outgoing president Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani, the country's Guardian Council as well as the Council of Experts.

"My government considers dialogue between civilisations in the present world essential and will avoid any action or behaviour causing tension. We will have relations with any government that observes our independence and respects our decisions within our national interests," Khatami said in a speech following his swearing in.
"But we will resist any power wishing to exercise dominance over us," he added in an apparent reference to the United States.
Referring to campaign promises to introduce social reforms, Khatami said he would "endeavour to establish and promote a lawful society which should apply to all aspects...of life".

Khatami, a 54-year-old Shi'ite Moslem cleric, was confirmed on Sunday as president by Iran's spiritual leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, three months after he won a landslide election victory against Nateq-Nouri.

His cabinet, which he must announce by August 18, is expected to be named this week. Proposed ministers must then be approved by parliament. The cabinet is expected to include representatives of various groups and at the same time seek to appease religious hardliners.
Analysts expect the first test of Khatami's future dealings with the conservative-dominated parliament to come when he seeks approval for his cabinet.
Khatami, a middle-level clergyman seen as a moderate in the Iranian context, did not indicate when he would present his cabinet to parliament or disclose the names of main candidates.
